normalized.prelim_summary: This 1972 Chevrolet C10 Cheyenne has been upgraded with a BluePrint 383ci stroker V8, modern EFI, and Wilwood brakes, driven only about 1,400 miles since the swap. The seller discloses minor paint chips and some door sill corrosion, but otherwise presents a well-documented, performance-built classic truck. The auction ended with the reserve not met at a high bid of $34,250.

evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a VIN, a clean TX title, a reserve auction closing Nov 4, and a seller who answers questions. The one attached photo shows glossy green/white paint and intact Cheyenne trim. Observed issues are disclosed passenger door-sill corrosion and paint chips. A bidder asserts the doors are not original 1972 parts and asks whether the bed was shortened, and that remains unresolved because the SPID photo the seller posted was not captured. The engine swap (BluePrint 383, Sniper 2 EFI) and the Wilwood brake work rest on seller statements, with no invoices in the captured text. Total mileage is effectively unknown behind a 5-digit odometer. Underside condition, tires, steering and front end, and compression all remain open. Against Jason's current brief, the truck is an automatic classic rather than the manual year-round daily he is shopping for.
evidence.next_action: Before Nov 4, ask the seller for the SPID and VIN-plate close-ups, underside lift photos, and the BluePrint/installer invoices, and confirm whether a mobile inspector in Bryan, TX can do a compression and lift inspection before the close.
